'''Paul David Neil Hebert''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|OC|FRSC}} (born 1947) is a Canadian [[biologist]]. He is founder and director of the [[Centre for Biodiversity Genomics]] at the [[University of Guelph]] in [[Ontario]], Canada. He applied the technique invented by [[Carl Woese]] and colleagues in the 1980s<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Woese |first1=C R |last2=Kandler |first2=O |last3=Wheelis |first3=M L |title=Towards a natural system of organisms: proposal for the domains Archaea, Bacteria, and Eucarya. |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |date=June 1990 |volume=87 |issue=12 |pages=4576–4579 |doi=10.1073/pnas.87.12.4576 |pmid=2112744 |pmc=54159 |bibcode=1990PNAS...87.4576W |doi-access=free }}</ref> to arthropods and called it [[DNA barcoding]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scienceline.org/2008/02/tweed-bio-dnabarcoding/|title=The Father of DNA Barcoding|date=2008-02-01|website=Scienceline|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.uoguelph.ca/2018/04/dna-barcoding-pioneer-wins-global-research-prize/|title=DNA Barcoding Pioneer Wins Global Research Prize|date=2018-04-24|website=U of G News|language=en|access-date=2019-01-24}}</ref>

Hebert holds the Tier 1 [[Canada Research Chair]] in molecular biodiversity<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=556|title=Canada Research Chairs|last=Government of Canada|first=Industry Canada|date=2012-11-29|website=www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca|access-date=2019-01-23}}</ref> at the University of Guelph where he is a [[tenure]]d professor in the Department of [[Integrative Biology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uoguelph.ca/ib/hebert|title=Paul Hebert {{!}} Department of Integrative Biology|website=www.uoguelph.ca|access-date=2019-01-23}}</ref> He is an [[Order of Canada|Officer of the Order of Canada]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gg.ca/en/honours/recipients/146-10772|title=Officer of the Order of Canada|last=Hebert|first=Paul}}</ref> a [[fellow]] of the [[Royal Society of Canada]], and received the 2018 [[Heineken Prizes|Heineken Prize]] for environmental sciences,<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/heineken-prizes/paul-d-n-hebert |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190522190622/https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/heineken-prizes/paul-d-n-hebert |title=Paul D.N. Hebert |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=22 May 2019}}</ref> and the 2020 [https://midoripress.net/en/topics/midorinews/5974/ MIDORI Prize for Biodiversity].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winners of the MIDORI Prize for Biodiversity 2020|url=https://midoripress.net/en/topics/midorinews/5974/|access-date=2020-09-02|website=The MIDORI Press|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2021, he was awarded the honorary degree of ''Doctor Honoris Causa'' at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (NTNU).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honorary Doctors - NTNU|url=https://www.ntnu.edu/phd/honorary-doctors|access-date=2021-09-29|website=www.ntnu.edu}}</ref> Hebert also holds honorary degrees from [[Western University (Canada)|Western University]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-06-13 |title=Western News - Hebert: Go forth and make magic |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2018/06/hebert-go-forth-make-magic/ |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=Western News |language=en-CA}}</ref> [[University of Windsor]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paul Hebert {{!}} DailyNews |url=https://www.uwindsor.ca/dailynews/rehse/electrical/tags/paul-hebert |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=www.uwindsor.ca}}</ref> and [[University of Waterloo]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-09-20 |title=Waterloo will honour adviser to Governor General at fall convocation |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/news/news/waterloo-will-honour-adviser-governor-general-fall-convocation |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=Waterloo News |language=en}}</ref> in Canada.

In 2025, he received the Sustainability Award, presented by the Nobel Sustainability Trust (NST) in cooperation with the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM), for outstanding research and development in the field of biodiversity. He developed [[DNA]] barcoding, a method to rapidly identify species, which is vital for global conservation efforts.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Sustainability Award 2025 |url=https://www.nobelsustainabilitytrust.org/the-sustainability-award-2025 |website=Nobel Sustainability Trust}}</ref>
